citation: AP162: A large-scale dataset for agricultural pest recognition, Computers and Electronics in Agriculture 237 (2025). https://github.com/SCNYDX-KL/AP162
licence: Academic research use only. Commercial use, redistribution and sublicensing are prohibited by the authors.
notes: AP162 labels at species level and splits larva from adult into separate classes. We merge the pair into one pest class and carry the stage in `life_stage`, because the advisory differs by stage (adults on a trap mean 'monitor and count'; larvae in the whorl mean 'treat the affected plants today') while the species identification does not.

The dataset's centre of gravity is East Asian, and a large share of its classes are forest, ornamental or stored-product pests. Those are excluded rather than force-fitted: training an Indian field model to recognise sycamore lace bug costs capacity and teaches the model confusions that cannot occur in the target fields.
`excluded` entries are deliberate, with a reason. Anything absent from BOTH maps is an error and the ingest will report it.
